note: CLASSIFICATION IS BY EFFECT, NEVER BY STATEMENT TYPE (docs/SPECIFICATION.md §2). All three statements are SelectStmt nodes. The first deletes rows through a data-modifying CTE and is PG009. The second moves a sequence through setval() and is PG010. Only the third is actually a read, and it stays PG027/UNKNOWN -- no permissive default was added, because the generalisation that would justify one is exactly the generalisation that is wrong. If this fixture ever grades the first two REVERSIBLE, a rule keyed on the node type has been added and the product is broken.
